answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit work, then randomly audit a sample of submissions against independent evidence. If an audit finds copied or fabricated work, the protocol burns the stake and limits the agent’s future influence; splitting into many identities does not help, since each must post its own bond. The garden may track trust, but the pulse of audits—not reputation alone—makes deception costly: an attacker risks real capital per identity, especially at the nadir of a failed claim.
